findings.title: Level-progress sync to apo-games.de 'cookies.php' over plain HTTP; server response trusted for unlock state
findings.code_excerpt: url = new URL(codebase + "cookies.php"); URLConnection con = url.openConnection(); ((HttpURLConnection) con).setRequestMethod("GET");
findings.entry_point: Network: HTTP response from http://www.apo-games.de/apoRelax/cookies.php, read in ApoHelp.loadData (ApoHelp.java:452-465); triggered at applet startup from ApoRelaxPanel.init (apoRelax/game/ApoRelaxPanel.java:93)
findings.sink: Integer.valueOf(load) then this.levelChooser.setMaxLevel(level) at ApoRelaxPanel.java:94-95; complementary write-back of progress via ApoHelp.saveData at ApoRelaxPanel.java:212
findings.data_path: ApoRelaxPanel.init() -> ApoHelp.loadData(new URL("http://www.apo-games.de/apoRelax/"), "level") -> URLConnection to cookies.php -> iStream.readLine() -> Integer.valueOf -> ApoRelaxLevelChooser.setMaxLevel (apoRelax/game/ApoRelaxLevelChooser.java:119-125). On each solved level: ApoRelaxGame.think (apoRelax/game/ApoRelaxGame.java:353) -> ApoRelaxPanel.setMaxLevel (ApoRelaxPanel.java:208-218) -> ApoHelp.saveData writes "SET=&name=level&value=N" in cleartext
findings.attack_scenario: Applet deployment only (B_APPLET=true is set solely in the ApoRelaxApplet constructor, apoRelax/ApoRelaxApplet.java:28). An on-path attacker (open Wi-Fi, ISP, compromised CDN/DNS for apo-games.de) intercepts the cleartext request to cookies.php and replies with an arbitrary integer, unlocking all levels; likewise they can suppress or forge the SET= progress upload. No authentication or TLS anywhere, and there is no user identity, so responses cannot even be bound to a player.
findings.preconditions: Game must run as applet (ApoRelaxApplet). The desktop entry point ApoRelaxMain (apoRelax/ApoRelaxMain.java) leaves B_APPLET=false (org/apogames/ApoConstants.java:12) and performs no network I/O at all. Given Java applets are obsolete, this is live only for historical deployments.
findings.validation_plan: Map www.apo-games.de to 127.0.0.1 in /etc/hosts, run a plain-HTTP listener logging requests. Launch the applet (or patch ApoConstants.B_APPLET=true before ApoRelaxPanel.init). Observer 1: plaintext request to /apoRelax/cookies.php containing body 'GET=&name=level' (proves no TLS/no integrity). Observer 2: reply with body '11' and confirm the level chooser renders buttons up to level 11 unlocked. Wireshark shows the entire exchange in cleartext.

findings.title: ApoClassLoader loads and instantiates classes from arbitrary file/URL paths - present but with zero call sites in this variant
findings.code_excerpt: URLClassLoader cl = new URLClassLoader( new URL[] { url } ); ... c = cl.loadClass( this.getClassname() ); ... return c.newInstance();
findings.entry_point: Whatever string is passed as 'path'/'classname' to the ApoClassLoader constructor (lines 19-22). In applet mode any URL is accepted (line 68: url = new URL(this.getPath())), in application mode any local directory/jar via new File(path).toURI().toURL() (line 66). In THIS variant the entry point does not exist: grep across all 56 files finds no instantiation of ApoClassLoader.
findings.sink: URLClassLoader construction + cl.loadClass(...) + c.newInstance() at lines 69-75, i.e. execution of attacker-chosen static/constructor code
findings.data_path: (potential) caller -> new ApoClassLoader(path, classname) -> getMyClass() -> URLClassLoader/loadClass/newInstance. No intermediate methods exist in this variant because no caller exists.
findings.attack_scenario: If any sibling variant (this class is shared cloned infrastructure) wires ApoClassLoader to user-editable config or a network path, an attacker who controls path+classname gets their class instantiated inside the game process = full code execution. As shipped in ApoRelax, an attacker gains nothing: the class is inert.
findings.preconditions: Requires a source modification adding a call such as new ApoClassLoader(attackerPath, attackerClass).getMyClass(); with B_APPLET=true the path may be a remote http(s) URL served without any signature or hash check.
findings.validation_plan: Reachability proof (negative): rg -n "new ApoClassLoader|getMyClass" --type java returns matches only inside ApoClassLoader.java itself. Danger proof (positive): compile Evil.java with a printing static initializer into dir/, run harness 'new ApoClassLoader(<dir-or-http-URL>, "Evil").getMyClass()' - constructor output proves arbitrary instantiation; serve the same .class over http://localhost:8000 with B_APPLET=true to prove remote loading.

findings.title: Cloned highscore client submits level blobs over plain HTTP to sibling variant's endpoint ('apoNotSoSimple') - dead code in ApoRelax
findings.code_excerpt: url = new URL(ApoConstants.HIGHSCORE_SAVEPHP); ... String content = "levelname=" + URLEncoder.encode(..."&username="... "&description=" ... "&solution=" ... "&level=" ...); printout.writeBytes(content);
findings.entry_point: Would be network responses parsed line-by-line in load() (ApoHighscore.java:170-183) into levelnames/usernames/descriptions/solution lists, and locally produced score data in save(). Endpoints are hardcoded at org/apogames/ApoConstants.java:21-22 to http://www.apo-games.de/apoNotSoSimple/get_highscore.php and save_highscore.php - a different game's endpoints, evidence of clone-and-own copying without adjustment.
findings.sink: urlConn.getOutputStream()/writeBytes (cleartext POST of level, solution, username) at ApoHighscore.java:86-120 and DataInputStream(urlConn.getInputStream()) at line 167 whose content lands unchecked in ArrayLists exposed via getters (lines 40-58)
findings.data_path: save(): byte[][][] level serialized digit-by-digit into myLevel (lines 88-99) -> URLEncoder -> DataOutputStream over http://. load(): response lines split modulo 5 into five parallel ArrayLists. In this variant NEITHER method is invoked: grep shows ApoHighscore referenced nowhere outside its own file; the UPLOAD button constants exist in apoRelax/game/ApoRelaxGame.java:30-31 but mouseButtonFunction (line 251) never handles 'game_upload'.
findings.attack_scenario: Were it wired up (as in sibling variants): a MITM forges save_highscore.php responses to inject arbitrary usernames/descriptions rendered in-game (stored-content spoofing), reads submitted solutions in transit, and can replay/fabricate scores because the protocol carries no signature, nonce, or TLS. Additionally, submissions from ApoRelax would pollute the apoNotSoSimple leaderboard due to the cloned constants.
findings.preconditions: Requires adding a call site (e.g. wiring the unused game_upload button). Note ApoConstants.B_ONLINE defaults true (ApoConstants.java:16), so only the missing caller blocks execution today.
findings.validation_plan: Negative: grep -rn 'ApoHighscore' --include='*.java' -> self-references only. Positive harness: hosts-point www.apo-games.de to localhost, call ApoHighscore.getInstance().load(); serve 10 crafted lines; observe getDescriptions()/getUsernames() populated with the forged strings. Wireshark simultaneously captures the plaintext POST body containing the serialized level and solution strings.

findings.title: Remote random-image fetch from zufallsbild.com (HTTP scrape + ImageIO.read of derived URL) trapped in dead else-branch behind tautological condition
findings.code_excerpt: if ((ApoConstants.B_APPLET) || (!ApoConstants.B_APPLET)) { return ...getRandomImage(); } else { String myUrl = "http://www.zufallsbild.com/"; ... BufferedImage iImage = ImageIO.read(new URL(imageString));
findings.entry_point: HTTP: HTML scraped from http://www.zufallsbild.com/ via url.openStream() (line 31); the code then walks backwards from every '.jpg' occurrence until a double-quote char (34) and concatenates the substring onto myUrl to build 'imageString', which is fetched and decoded (lines 33-52)
findings.sink: ImageIO.read(new URL(imageString)) at line 51 - decodes bytes from a URL assembled out of attacker-influenceable page text; upstream Reader on openStream() at line 31
findings.data_path: getRandomLevel() line 25 evaluates '(B_APPLET) || (!B_APPLET)' which is a TAUTOLOGY (always true), so the else block lines 27-61 can never execute under any configuration. If the condition were fixed to 'if (B_APPLET)' the path would be: getRandomLevel -> InputStreamReader(url.openStream()) -> char-by-char scan -> imageString -> new URL(imageString) -> ImageIO.read -> ApoRelaxLevelGeneration.getImage/getRandomLevel.
findings.attack_scenario: As shipped: unreachable, no attacker gain. If re-enabled: anyone controlling DNS/routing for zufallsbild.com (dead domain, trivially registrable) serves HTML whose '.jpg'-adjacent text steers imageString to an attacker URL, making the client issue GETs to arbitrary hosts (SSRF-style beacon) and feeding chosen bytes into the ImageIO decoder of every player clicking 'random level'.
findings.preconditions: Source edit changing the line-25 tautology into a real condition; plus control of zufallsbild.com or the victim's DNS/network. Domain status would need re-checking at test time.
findings.validation_plan: Unreachability proof: evaluate the guard - (x || !x) == true for any B_APPLET, so the else is dead code; confirm via coverage (JaCoCo shows lines 27-61 never executed after playing a random level). Behavior proof: in a scratch copy replace the guard with 'if (!ApoConstants.B_APPLET)', add '127.0.0.1 www.zufallsbild.com' to /etc/hosts, serve an HTML page whose first '.jpg' context yields '/evil.jpg'; observe the client fetching http://www.zufallsbild.com/evil.jpg and decoding it into tiles.

findings.title: Editor parses arbitrary user-selected image file with ImageIO (extension-only filter, no size/format limits)
findings.code_excerpt: } else { try { if ( ApoConstants.B_APPLET ) { img = ImageIO.read(new URL(pic)); } else { img = ImageIO.read(new File(pic)); }
findings.entry_point: File chosen in JFileChooser: ApoRelaxEditor.loadImage (apoRelax/game/ApoRelaxEditor.java:221-232, key 'L' at line 180-181 or LOAD button gated !B_APPLET at line 192) passes the selected absolute path through ApoRelaxImages.getImage(path,true) (apoRelax/ApoRelaxImages.java:40-42) and ApoImageFromValue.getImageFromPath (org/apogames/image/ApoImageFromValue.java:47-49)
findings.sink: ImageIO.read(new File(pic)) at ApoImage.java:93 - full decode of untrusted file bytes by the JDK image parsers (JPEG/PNG/GIF/BMP readers). The 400px cap in ApoRelaxLevelGeneration.getImage (apoRelax/level/ApoRelaxLevelGeneration.java:491-511) applies only AFTER complete decoding.
findings.data_path: keyReleased VK_L / LOAD button -> loadImage() -> getSelectedFile().getPath() -> ApoRelaxImages.getImage -> ApoImageFromValue.getImageFromPath -> ApoImage.getPic -> ApoImage.getImage(pic, bLoad=true) -> ImageIO.read(File). Filter is extension-only: ApoFileFilter.accept (org/apogames/help/ApoFileFilter.java:70-86) checks the filename suffix against {jpg,png,bmp,gif,jpeg} set at apoRelax/ApoRelaxComponent.java:34; content is never validated. The sibling branch ImageIO.read(new URL(pic)) at ApoImage.java:91 is NOT reachable here: loadImage is only invoked when B_APPLET==false.
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker social-engineers a victim into opening a hostile 'puzzle picture': (a) a decompression-bomb PNG (e.g. 50000x50000) exhausts heap during decode, freezing/crashing the game; (b) on an unpatched JRE, malformed JPEG/PNG chunks targeting known ImageIO CVEs yield client-side code execution. Gain ranges from DoS to RCE depending on the victim's JVM - bounded by the fact that the user must hand-pick the file.
findings.preconditions: Desktop run (B_APPLET=false); victim must select the attacker-supplied file in the editor dialog. Extension filter is cosmetic - renaming keeps the dialog happy, and ImageIO sniffs magic bytes regardless of name.
findings.validation_plan: Generate a 60000x60000 all-blue PNG (decompression bomb), press L in the editor and open it: heap climbs hundreds of MB and UI stalls BEFORE any downscale occurs (add a breakpoint/log at ApoImage.java:93 vs ApoRelaxLevelGeneration.getImage:495 to show the cap comes too late). For the parser angle, feed a PNG fuzzed with a known pre-2022 ImageIO CVE sample against a matching old JRE and observe the crash/exception inside ImageIO.read.

categories_checked_and_absent: untrusted_deserialization (no java.io.ObjectInputStream anywhere in the 56 files; no other deserialization framework)

path_traversal (no file path is ever built from network/level/user input; only JAR resources and the hardcoded System.getProperty("user.dir") sound path in AudioPlayer.java:70, itself dead code behind 'private final boolean BInJAR = true')
unsafe_native_call (no System.load, no JNI native methods, no Runtime.exec/ProcessBuilder - verified by pattern sweep)
credential_or_secret_exposure (no passwords, tokens, keys, or identity material exist in this variant; highscore payloads carry no credentials because no caller exists)
notes:
Tree-layout caveat: the stated SOURCE ROOT contains only a mirror of the user's home path; actual project root is Users/eliahilse/Documents/GitHub/B/apogames/Java/ApoRelax (all paths above are relative to it). 22 files were opened and read; the remaining 34 (pure UI/entity/render/input code such as ApoButton, ApoEntity, ApoMouse, scale helpers, menus) were swept with exhaustive greps for every sink class (network, stream/file IO, classloading, reflection, digest, exec, serialization) with no further hits.

This is the cleanest variant shape-wise: ApoRelax has NO persistent save files, NO custom level/replay/binary format parsing (.mar/.skunk/.rep style formats of siblings are absent), and the desktop application (ApoRelaxMain) performs zero network I/O - levels are generated in-code from JAR-bundled images (ApoRelaxLevelGeneration.initImageArray). All network surface is gated behind B_APPLET (set only in ApoRelaxApplet's constructor).

Large inventory of dead cloned infrastructure - key clone-propagation evidence: (1) ApoClassLoader: zero callers (finding 02); (2) ApoHighscore: zero callers, and its hardcoded endpoints still point at SIBLING GAME apoNotSoSimple (ApoConstants.java:21-22); (3) ApoHelp.getMd5Digest MD5 helper (ApoHelp.java:301-310): zero callers - the weak_integrity_check pattern exists only as an uncalled remnant; (4) abstract ApoIO (readLevel/writeLevel incl. the HttpURLConnection branch at ApoIO.java:40-43): no subclass, no callers; (5) ApoCopy file-copy utility: zero callers; (6) ApoImageScale/ApoRawScale2x/3x: no external callers; (7) AudioPlayer.java:67-71 remote-audio and user.dir branches unreachable because BInJAR is final true (line 19); (8) ApoRelaxGame defines UPLOAD button/time constants (lines 30-31,46-47) but no upload handler exists. Also notable developer artifacts: the tautological guard (finding 04) and debug System.out.println of internal coordinates in ApoRelaxEditor.mouseButtonFunction (lines 196-210).

Client-side trust: desktop progress (maxLevel, ApoRelaxLevelChooser.java:29,119-125) lives only in memory - trivially cheatable via memory editing, but nothing is persisted or submitted, so there is no integrity target worth reporting as a separate finding; the applet-side trust issue is covered in finding 01. Resource exhaustion appears only as the image-decode vector folded into finding 05.
